command: cytoscape({ container: <div 1200x900>, elements: file.elements, style: file.style, layout: { name: "preset" } }); after a forced render: renderer.drawElements(svgContext, z-sorted elements) at the view's pan and zoom, as cytoscape-svg's cy.svg({ full: false }) does
how: Cytoscape.js's own canvas renderer (renderer.drawElements over the z-sorted elements, at the view's pan and zoom) replayed onto an svgcanvas context, as the cytoscape-svg extension's cy.svg({ full: false }) does; the Path2D objects Cytoscape.js fills by reference are recorded and replayed as SVG paths. cytoscape-svg itself is not used: its bundled canvas2svg drops shapes (a node's path commands after the previous label's fillText land on the <text>), and it turns path caching off, where Cytoscape.js draws a rounded polygon without beginPath() and joins it to the shape before; both left node shapes missing or smeared in its SVG. The SVG is the viewport a user of this file sees, not the whole graph. The svgcanvas context is corrected where it departs from a canvas (SVG_CONTEXT in web-oracle.mjs): the current path survives save() and fillText(), a text keeps its blanks (xml:space), a Path2D argument is replayed (with the paths added to it), a clip keeps its evenodd rule, gradients and 1-wide or dashed strokes follow the transform, and a text outline is not scaled twice; each was checked against Chromium's own screenshot of the same drawing. A shadow (shadowColor, shadowBlur, shadowOffsetX / Y) is recorded as an feDropShadow filter in device pixels. Not recorded: globalCompositeOperation (a Cytoscape.js double border draws as one ring); a glyph the pinned fonts lack (a vis-network icon) rasterizes as a box where Chromium draws nothing.
